who_what.text: The repository README identifies this as a collection of 30 separate Jupyter notebooks. Technique 30 presents a production-memory walkthrough built from illustrative local Python stores and describes Redis, Postgres/pgvector, and graph services as production replacements. This review treats it as educational material, not as a single production memory service.

architecture.text: The notebook's MemoryRecord stores an ID, user ID, content, optional embedding, timestamps, access count, importance, tier, optional TTL, tags, a PII-redacted flag, token estimate, and optional compressed bytes. HotTierCache, WarmTierStore, and ColdTierArchive use in-process dictionaries and per-user indexes; cold content is compressed with zlib. These inspected classes simulate Redis-like and Postgres/pgvector-like behavior.

GraphEdge stores source, relation, target, user ID, timestamp, and an optional memory ID. GraphRelationshipStore keeps edges in a Python list and adjacency map, and offers relation lookup and breadth-first neighbor traversal. The README describes fact extraction, embeddings, PII handling, budgets, and cost/observability concerns as the wider technique design.

behavior.text: Write: the inspected stores expose put in hot/warm tiers and archive in cold storage. Hot writes set a default TTL and, at per-user capacity, remove and demote the least recently accessed record. Warm writes store by record ID and add that ID to the user's index. No general correction-history or version-resolution contract was established in the inspected store sections.

Retrieval: WarmTierStore.search requires user_id, scans the user's indexed records, skips records without usable embeddings, computes cosine similarity, sorts descending, and returns at most k results. Hot get and cold retrieve use record IDs. The technique README describes hot-to-warm-to-cold search and promotion, but the end-to-end orchestration was not traced through the whole notebook.

Deletion: the inspected hot, warm, cold, and graph classes each define delete_user. They remove user records or graph edges from their local in-memory stores; graph deletion rebuilds the adjacency map. The README describes a broader right-to-forget flow with audit logging, but this review did not trace a complete orchestrated deletion path or external-store deletion.

Scope: per-user indexes constrain warm search and user-record listing. Graph query, hot get(record_id), and cold retrieve(record_id) do not accept a user ID, so those inspected lookup methods do not themselves enforce user isolation. No runtime isolation check was performed.

Provenance: the record model includes user ID and timestamps; GraphEdge can retain a source memory ID. The inspected record structure does not show trust state or source citation fields. Claim-level evidence and answer citations remain unverified.

metrics.evidence: Source code observations do not establish gold-case retrieval correctness or calibrated abstention, and no system probes were run.
The inspected store sections do not establish correction history or stale-value resolution; no post-correction probes were run.
Local delete_user methods are visible, but end-to-end deletion completeness and post-delete leakage were not verified or measured.
Some methods use per-user indexes while ID/entity lookup methods inspected do not take a user ID; no cross-scope runtime probes were performed.
The source structures reviewed do not establish answer-claim citations or adjudicated evidence support.
The README discusses latency goals and the cache code keeps counters, but no latency or write-to-recall observations were collected.
The record has an approximate token field and cold storage counts compressed byte differences; these are source-visible structures, not measured workload token, cost, or storage outcomes.

HotTierCache defines hit, miss, eviction, and expiration counters plus a hit_rate property. ColdTierArchive tracks a compressed-byte difference. These do not provide measured latency distributions or establish monitoring coverage across all operations.

limits.text: This bounded review inspected the repository README, technique 30 README, and notebook model/store sections through the graph store. Later notebook cells and full orchestration were not traced. The README describes horizontal sharding and distributed deployment as additional infrastructure beyond the single-node example.

The reviewed notebook sections use in-memory dictionaries and lists; they do not demonstrate production Redis/Postgres persistence, concurrency, authorization, backup recovery, or reliability. Unknown means not established by this inspection, not impossible or absent from every notebook.

benchmark.text: Benchmark status: not_run. No system code, notebook, benchmark workload, or tests were executed for this review. The project status record is not a result for this system and planned fixture counts are not measured denominators.
